hero.headline: House passes $70 billion immigration enforcement funding through end of Trump term
hero.body:
The House of Representatives approved legislation providing $70 billion to fund immigration enforcement agencies through the remainder of President Trump's term, resolving a months-long funding dispute that had previously forced the Department of Homeland Security to shut down operations.

The Secure America Act passed in a 214-212 vote largely along party lines. All Democrats opposed the measure, as did independent Kevin Kiley who aligns with Republicans. The Senate had approved the bill the previous week.

The funding allocates $38 billion to Immigration and Customs Enforcement, $26 billion to Customs and Border Protection, and $5 billion to the Department of Homeland Security overall. The money extends through September 2029. The legislation now awaits President Trump's signature.

Republicans argued the bill was necessary to support border security and immigration law enforcement operations. The GOP caucus continued to back Trump's immigration agenda throughout the debate.

Democrats raised concerns about the legislation's lack of congressional oversight mechanisms. They argued that Congress had surrendered its oversight role by providing such extensive funding without adequate accountability measures in place.

The extended funding impasse had lasted for months as lawmakers debated both the scope of immigration enforcement spending and the level of congressional oversight required. The passage of this bill ended that standoff.

The approval of the measure highlights the deep political divide over immigration policy between the two parties. Republicans characterized the funding as essential to securing the border and enforcing immigration law. Democrats maintained their position that the bill failed to include sufficient safeguards to ensure accountability.

The bill's passage in the House came after similar approval in the Senate, setting the stage for Trump's expected signature. The legislation represents a significant financial commitment to immigration enforcement operations moving forward.

The vote reflects the current composition of Congress, where Republicans hold enough seats to pass legislation along party lines with minimal Democratic support. The narrow 214-212 margin demonstrates the contentious nature of the debate, with even one Republican-aligned independent joining Democrats in opposition.

This funding decision occurs as immigration enforcement has become a central focus of the Trump administration's policy agenda. The resources will support ongoing operations by ICE and Border Patrol through the remainder of Trump's presidential term.

The resolution of the funding impasse removes an obstacle that had created uncertainty for immigration enforcement agencies over an extended period. With the bill now moving toward the president for signature, these agencies can operate with clear funding authorization through 2029.

cards.headline: U.S. Launches Military Strikes on Iran After Helicopter Downed
cards.body:
The United States military launched retaliatory strikes against Iran on Tuesday after an Apache helicopter gunship went down near the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump confirmed that Iranian forces were responsible for downing the aircraft and stated that the country "must, of necessity, respond to this attack."

U.S. Central Command said Trump directed the military to begin strikes at 10pm UK time on Tuesday. According to U.S. media citing White House officials, the strikes targeted radar and air defense facilities along the Strait of Hormuz. The Pentagon characterized the operation as "a proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression" and signaled that the U.S. was not seeking a return to full-scale war with Iran.

The helicopter went down at approximately 3:30am local time off the coast of Oman while on patrol. In a notable rescue operation, an unmanned drone boat located the two aviators after they spent about two hours in the water. U.S. Central Command spokesperson Captain Tim Hawkins said this was the first known drone rescue at sea by the U.S. military. The vessel used in the rescue, called a Corsair, measures 24 feet in length. Trump downplayed the incident in an interview with the Wall Street Journal, stating that the strike on the helicopter "wasn't a big deal" and that the "pilot is fine."

Military officials did not disclose what caused the Apache to crash, saying the incident remained under investigation.

The strikes come after tensions escalated dramatically across the region. Iranian and Israeli forces exchanged fire on Monday, dealing a significant blow to a ceasefire that the U.S. and Iran had announced in April. Israeli state television reported that Israeli attacks killed at least two members of Iran's air defense units. Concurrently, Israeli forces have intensified military operations in southern Lebanon against Hezbollah, the Iranian-backed militia.

Before accusing Iran of downing the helicopter, Trump had expressed optimism about negotiations with Iran, telling reporters there was "a good chance" of signing a deal within "two or three days." However, he provided no specific details supporting this assessment. He added that while bombing Iran would be possible, it could kill many people and disrupt the Strait of Hormuz for months.

Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, responded to the situation by saying: "We prefer the language of diplomacy, but we speak other languages far more fluently. Break your commitments, and we'll switch to what we speak best." Tehran has not yet indicated whether it plans to retaliate for the U.S. strikes.

Apache helicopters have served as key assets for American forces enforcing a blockade on Iranian crude oil shipments in an effort to pressure Tehran into a negotiated settlement.

cards.headline: Israeli Forces Strike Lebanese City of Tyre After Evacuation Warning
cards.teaser: Israel launched air strikes on the ancient coastal city of Tyre in southern Lebanon, with at least eight people killed.
cards.body:
Israeli air strikes targeted the Lebanese city of Tyre, prompting evacuation orders for residents of the ancient coastal city. The strikes proceeded despite Iran's warning to Israel that it could resume hostilities if attacks on its Lebanese ally Hezbollah continue.

Christian leaders in Tyre have called for urgent international intervention following the Israeli military warning. The city, which has been inhabited for thousands of years and holds UNESCO World Heritage status, faces significant displacement as residents respond to evacuation orders.

cards.headline: Social Security retirement benefits face 22 percent cut by 2032 without congressional action
cards.body:
The trust fund that finances Social Security retirement benefits for approximately 68 million Americans is expected to run out of money by 2032, one year sooner than previously estimated, according to a report from the program's trustees. If Congress does not intervene before the fund depletes, beneficiaries could experience an automatic reduction of roughly 22 percent in their monthly benefit payments.

The accelerated timeline reflects mounting financial strain on Social Security as the baby boomer generation continues retiring and the ratio of working people paying into the system declines relative to retirees receiving benefits. The program depends on payroll taxes collected from current workers to fund payments to retirees. This demographic shift has created a growing gap between money coming in and money going out.

Social Security has served as a fundamental source of retirement income for millions of Americans since its creation in 1935. The program has consistently paid scheduled benefits throughout its history, but the projected shortfall signals an urgent challenge ahead. If the trust fund becomes depleted, benefits would not vanish entirely. Instead, payments would be limited to revenue from incoming payroll taxes, triggering the automatic cuts.

Congress has multiple options to address the funding gap. Lawmakers could raise the payroll tax rate, increase the income cap that payroll taxes apply to, reduce benefits for higher earners, raise the retirement age, or pursue a combination of these approaches. Addressing Social Security remains politically challenging, however, since the program touches virtually every American family and proposed changes typically encounter resistance from various groups.

The trustees' report creates pressure on lawmakers to act within the next six years to avert automatic benefit reductions. Earlier projections had suggested Congress had until 2033 to resolve the funding issue, but the accelerated timeline narrows the window for legislative action. The sooner depletion date increases the urgency for policymakers to reach a bipartisan agreement that would stabilize the program's finances while protecting benefits for both current and future beneficiaries.

The situation demands that Congress balance several competing interests. Younger workers worry about whether benefits will exist when they retire. Current retirees depend on stable payments for daily living expenses. Businesses object to higher payroll taxes, while higher earners may resist benefit reductions or tax increases. Finding common ground across these groups requires difficult political negotiations.

Experts emphasize that waiting longer makes any solution more painful. Early action allows for gradual adjustments spread over many years, while delayed action forces more dramatic changes concentrated in a shorter timeframe. The trustees' report serves as a warning that Congress cannot indefinitely postpone addressing Social Security's structural challenges. The clock is ticking toward a decision point that will shape retirement security for millions of Americans.

cards.headline: Trump signals Iran deal still possible despite strikes
cards.teaser: The president indicated he believes a diplomatic agreement with Iran remains achievable despite launching retaliatory airstrikes.
cards.body:
President Trump confirmed that Iran shot down a U.S. Army Apache helicopter and said the U.S. must respond. On Tuesday at 5 p.m. ET, the U.S. military launched retaliatory strikes against Iranian targets.

Despite the military action, Trump indicated he believes a deal with Iran remains possible. The president has sporadically threatened additional military action since February but has avoided full-scale attacks, suggesting he views the strikes as a measured response that keeps diplomatic negotiations open.

cards.headline: Oil prices reach seven-week low after Israel and Iran halt attacks
cards.teaser: Crude prices declined as tensions eased between the two countries.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell to their lowest level in seven weeks after Israel and Iran agreed to stop military strikes against each other. The decline reflected reduced concerns about supply disruptions from a wider conflict in the Middle East.

The agreement between the two countries removed a risk premium that had supported higher crude prices in recent weeks. Energy markets had priced in the possibility of attacks on oil infrastructure or shipping routes, and the halt in hostilities lowered those concerns.

cards.headline: SpaceX initial public offering attracts demand four times subscription size
cards.teaser: The space company's stock offering has generated significantly more investor interest than shares available.
cards.body:
SpaceX's initial public offering has drawn demand approaching four times the number of shares being offered, according to a source familiar with the matter. The level of oversubscription indicates strong investor appetite for the space exploration and satellite company.

The IPO has reportedly attracted approximately $250 billion in orders for what is valued as a $75 billion offering. The allocation for retail investors remains undetermined as the company finalizes the share distribution among institutional and individual buyers.

cards.headline: Violent Protests Erupt in Belfast After Stabbing Attack
cards.teaser: Anti-immigration protests turned violent in Northern Ireland following a brutal knife attack, with demonstrators setting vehicles on fire.
cards.body:
Police in Belfast arrested a 30-year-old Sudanese man in connection with a stabbing attack that was recorded and spread rapidly online. The suspect was charged with assaulting another man in the incident that sparked widespread unrest across the city.

Protesters set vehicles ablaze and stormed at least one residence during demonstrations that spread across Belfast. Masked individuals entered homes, with witnesses describing panic as they targeted properties. U.K. leaders urged calm as the violence escalated, with calls circulating on social media for additional anti-immigration protests throughout Northern Ireland.

cards.headline: UK and Allies Impose Sanctions on Networks Supporting West Bank Settler Violence
cards.teaser: Britain and allied nations announced sanctions targeting groups that enable violence by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.
cards.body:
The United Kingdom and partner countries have sanctioned networks accused of enabling settler violence in the West Bank. France is barring far-right Israeli Minister Bezalel Smotrich from entering the country as part of these coordinated measures.

Israel has condemned the sanctions as "disgraceful." The actions target organizations and individuals linked to violent actions by Israeli settlers against Palestinians in the occupied territory, reflecting international concern over escalating violence in the region.

cards.headline: Trump Family Resort Plan in Albania Faces EU Environmental Scrutiny
cards.teaser: A luxury resort project in Albania linked to Jared Kushner threatens to violate European Union environmental law, prompting intervention from Brussels.
cards.body:
The European Union pressed Albanian authorities over a planned luxury resort developed by Jared Kushner, citing potential violations of EU environmental regulations. The project, located on a protected beach, has drawn opposition from local residents and conservation groups. Ivanka Trump is involved in planning the resort development.

The Albanian government's handling of the project could affect the country's bid to join the European Union. Mass protests have erupted in Albania over the resort plan, with conservationists raising concerns about development on environmentally protected coastline. The controversy highlights tensions between economic development ambitions and environmental protection standards required for EU membership.

cards.headline: Myanmar Rebels Lose Ground as Military Forces Conscription
cards.teaser: Rebel forces in Myanmar are losing territory as the military government intensifies forced recruitment into the army.
cards.body:
Rebel fighters in Myanmar are losing territory to government troops as the military junta intensifies forced recruitment to strengthen its armed forces. The BBC's Quentin Sommerville traveled to frontline positions without government permission to document how the conflict is unfolding across the country.

The civil war has continued since the military seized power, with various ethnic armed organizations and pro-democracy forces engaged in armed resistance against the junta. The military's expanded conscription efforts reflect the escalating nature of the ongoing conflict.

cards.headline: Somali Referee Denied U.S. Entry for World Cup
cards.teaser: Omar Abdulkadir Artan said he had proper documentation but was turned back, ending his chance to become the first Somali to referee at the tournament.
cards.body:
Omar Abdulkadir Artan was set to make history as the first Somali national to referee a World Cup match. Instead, U.S. immigration officials turned him away at the border, dashing his long-held dream to officiate at the tournament being held in the United States.

In his first public comments since the denial, Artan expressed his disappointment over being blocked from entry. He insisted he had all the necessary documentation in order. His case reflects broader concerns about enhanced immigration scrutiny affecting match officials and team members attempting to enter the country for the World Cup.

cards.headline: Three federal judges face misconduct allegations across different states
cards.teaser: Misconduct allegations against three judges in separate states are increasing scrutiny on how the federal judiciary polices behavior within its own ranks.
cards.body:
Three judges are facing misconduct allegations in three different states, drawing renewed attention to how the federal judiciary investigates and addresses misconduct among its members.

The cases are intensifying scrutiny of the judiciary's internal accountability system, which has long faced criticism for its lack of transparency and questions about its effectiveness in holding judges responsible for their actions.

cards.headline: White House to close press access during UFC event unless organization provides credentials
cards.teaser: The White House will not provide press access during an upcoming UFC fight, leaving credential decisions to the fighting organization.
cards.body:
The White House will restrict reporter access during a UFC fight event unless the UFC organization itself grants press credentials—a departure from standard White House press protocols.

Extensive road closures are planned across Washington for the event. A Trump-backed super PAC is hosting a fundraiser the day before, with tickets priced at $1 million per person. The UFC is managing the logistical challenges of staging an octagon fight at the White House.

cards.headline: Trump considers replacing Pulte as Director of National Intelligence
cards.teaser: The White House is weighing a replacement for Trump's Director of National Intelligence pick following a meeting between Trump and Speaker Johnson.
cards.body:
President Trump is not expected to take immediate action on his Director of National Intelligence pick following a meeting with Speaker Johnson. Senate Majority Leader Thune indicated the White House is considering replacing Pulte in the role as a longer-term decision.

Trump has pressed Pulte to remove intelligence community employees. The uncertainty surrounding the DNI position has sparked broader questions about the future direction of the intelligence office itself.

cards.headline: Texas teen convicted of murdering rival team athlete at high school track meet
cards.teaser: A jury found Karmelo Anthony, 19, guilty of murdering 17-year-old Austin Metcalf in a fatal stabbing at a high school track meet.
cards.body:
A Texas teenager was convicted of murder Tuesday after fatally stabbing a 17-year-old track athlete from a rival high school during a meet. The case drew national attention in the Dallas suburb where both students attended different schools.

The jury reached its guilty verdict following the week-long trial. Jurors are now deliberating on the sentence for the defendant.

cards.headline: West Ham co-owner David Sullivan banned from contact with women's and youth teams since 2023
cards.teaser: The Football Association opened a safeguarding investigation that resulted in David Sullivan being prohibited from contact with West Ham's women's and youth teams.
cards.body:
David Sullivan, West Ham's co-chair, has stood down ahead of allegations concerning his private life, which he denies. The club is currently in turmoil following these developments.

Sullivan has been restricted from contact with West Ham's women's and youth teams since 2023 following a safeguarding investigation by the Football Association.

cards.headline: Serena Williams wins on comeback after nearly four years away from tennis
cards.teaser: Serena Williams returned to competitive tennis at Queen's Club after 1,375 days away from the sport and won her match.
cards.body:
Serena Williams made a successful return to competitive tennis at Queen's Club after 1,375 days away from the sport. The legendary player demonstrated the skill and form that defined her championship-winning career during the comeback match.

The return marks a significant moment for one of tennis's most decorated athletes as she steps back onto the professional circuit.

The IPO has reportedly attracted approximately $250 billion in orders for what is valued as a $75 billion offering. The allocation for retail investors remains undetermined as the company finalizes the share distribution among institutional and individual buyers.

cards.headline: TSMC signals possible price increases as production costs rise
cards.teaser: A senior executive at the world's largest chipmaker discussed pricing pressure from rising expenses.
cards.body:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company has not ruled out raising prices as it contends with rising production costs. In a rare interview, a senior TSMC executive addressed how these cost pressures could ripple through the semiconductor industry and affect electronics prices globally.

The executive also discussed the artificial intelligence boom's impact on chip demand and the geopolitical factors reshaping the semiconductor supply chain. As the world's largest chipmaker and a critical supplier to major technology companies, TSMC's pricing decisions carry significant implications for the broader electronics industry.

cards.headline: General Motors plans battery production for energy storage market
cards.teaser: The automaker will manufacture batteries for electric utilities and data centers as electric vehicle sales slow.
cards.body:
General Motors announced plans to develop energy storage batteries for use by electric utilities, data centers, and other commercial customers. The move follows a similar strategy by Tesla and comes as the company's electric vehicle sales have not met earlier projections.

GM will produce sodium-ion battery cells specifically for the energy storage market rather than for electric vehicles. The batteries are designed to help manage fluctuations in power supply and demand, serving industries that require backup power systems and grid stabilization capabilities.

cards.headline: Stock markets decline on technology sector concerns and geopolitical uncertainty
cards.teaser: Equity indexes fell as investors reacted to developments in the technology industry and international tensions.
cards.body:
Stock markets in Asia and Europe fell on Monday following a sharp sell-off in US technology stocks the previous week. Investors are concerned about the ability of artificial intelligence-focused companies to fund their substantial spending plans.

Oil prices rose after Iran and Israel exchanged strikes, reducing hopes for a near-term reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The renewed Middle East conflict has dampened market sentiment despite earlier expectations for tension to ease.

cards.headline: Kalshi adds disclosure requirements to combat insider trading
cards.teaser: The prediction betting platform will require some users to reveal employment information under new rules.
cards.body:
Kalshi announced it will require certain users to disclose job details as part of new measures to address insider trading on its platform. The prediction betting site implemented the policy after facing issues with traders potentially using non-public information.

The changes target users whose employment could give them access to information relevant to prediction markets hosted on the platform. Kalshi operates a regulated exchange where users can place bets on future events ranging from economic data releases to political outcomes.

cards.headline: FDA approves new sunscreen ingredient after more than two decades
cards.teaser: The ingredient has been used in Europe and Asia for years but is new to the American market.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration approved a new sunscreen ingredient, marking the first such approval in more than 20 years. The ingredient has been available in European and Asian markets for years but required separate approval for use in the United States.

The FDA's decision expands the options available to sunscreen manufacturers in the United States. The ingredient had undergone safety testing and review before receiving authorization for use in consumer products sold in America.

hero.headline: NASA names four astronauts for Artemis III moon landing mission in 2027
hero.body:
NASA has announced the crew of four astronauts selected for the Artemis III mission, marking a major milestone in the agency's plan to return humans to the moon. The crew will launch in 2027 for a two-week mission to low Earth orbit that will test critical systems before a planned lunar landing on Artemis IV in 2028.

The Artemis III crew consists of NASA astronaut and commander Randy Bresnik, European Space Agency pilot Luca Parmitano from Italy, and NASA mission specialists Frank Rubio and Andre Douglas. The all-male crew will practice docking their Orion capsule with lunar landers developed by private companies SpaceX and Blue Origin during their orbital mission.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman described the group as part of "Earth's first starfleet" as he unveiled the crew and detailed the next stages of the agency's moon program. The Artemis III mission represents a significant step forward in testing the systems and procedures needed for eventual human landings on the lunar surface.

The Artemis program has already achieved historic milestones. The recent Artemis II mission, which launched earlier this year, completed a record-breaking journey around the moon. That crewed flight surpassed the maximum distance achieved by Apollo 13, traveling more than 250,000 miles from Earth. The four astronauts on Artemis II were the first lunar travelers since Apollo 17 in 1972, and the mission included historic achievements including sending the first person of color, the first woman, and the first non-American on a lunar mission.

During their five-day journey around the moon, the Artemis II crew experienced remarkable moments. Commander Reid Wiseman and his crewmates captured stunning images of Earth and witnessed the lunar far side from closer than any humans since the Apollo program. Despite the spectacular views, the mission also dealt with practical challenges, including a malfunctioning toilet that caused problems throughout the flight.

The Artemis program uses NASA's Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft, representing years of development following significant delays and cost overruns. The Space Launch System finally achieved its inaugural crewed flight with Artemis II after being rolled back to its hangar for repairs multiple times before launch.

Future Artemis missions will focus on the lunar south pole region, an area of scientific interest that differs from the Apollo landing sites near the moon's equator. The south pole contains permanently shadowed craters that may hold water ice, a resource that could support future exploration and establish a permanent lunar base.

The progression of Artemis missions demonstrates NASA's commitment to a multi-decade exploration program involving international partners and commercial companies. These missions will test capabilities needed for longer-duration stays on the moon and eventual missions beyond Earth orbit, laying the groundwork for human exploration of Mars.

cards.headline: Commonwealth Fusion publishes physics case for 400 megawatt fusion reactor
cards.teaser: The company released five peer-reviewed papers detailing the design and expected performance of its planned fusion power plant.
cards.body:
Commonwealth Fusion Systems published a set of five peer-reviewed papers that update the design of its planned fusion reactor and model its expected output. The papers make the physics case for a reactor capable of producing 400 megawatts of power.

The publications represent an effort to provide scientific validation for the company's reactor design. Fusion power attempts to replicate the energy-producing reactions that occur in the sun, a goal that has remained elusive despite decades of research. The papers detail technical specifications and performance projections for the planned facility.

cards.headline: Starlink introduces $10 monthly hardware fee, raises service prices
cards.teaser: SpaceX's satellite internet service switched from one-time hardware purchases to a monthly fee while also increasing subscription costs.
cards.body:
Starlink implemented a $10 monthly hardware fee, moving away from its previous model of one-time equipment purchases. The change affects how customers pay for the satellite dishes and routers needed to access the service.

The company also raised its service prices by $5 to $10, depending on the plan. Starlink represents SpaceX's largest revenue generator and provides satellite internet access to areas with limited traditional broadband options. The pricing adjustments apply to new and existing customers under the updated billing structure.

cards.headline: Microsoft patches zero-day vulnerabilities disclosed by security researcher
cards.teaser: The company fixed a security flaw after a researcher with whom it has had conflicts made the vulnerability public.
cards.body:
Microsoft released patches for a zero-day vulnerability disclosed by a security researcher. The fix addresses a security flaw that was made public before Microsoft had issued a patch, a situation known as a zero-day disclosure.

A separate zero-day vulnerability also disclosed by the researcher, known as Nightmare Eclipse, appears to have been patched as well. The fixes come amid what has been described as a heated rivalry between Microsoft and the researcher. Zero-day vulnerabilities pose security risks because they can be exploited before defenses are in place.

cards.headline: GM develops sodium-ion batteries for data centers and grid storage
cards.teaser: General Motors is creating a new battery chemistry intended for use beyond electric vehicles, including AI data centers.
cards.body:
General Motors is developing sodium-ion batteries designed for data centers and factory operations. Unlike the lithium-ion batteries standard in electric vehicles and consumer electronics, this new chemistry uses different materials better suited for large-scale stationary storage applications.

The move signals GM's expansion beyond automotive batteries as data centers increasingly need energy storage solutions to manage power demands from AI applications and provide backup capacity for the grid.

cards.headline: Anthropic restricts Fable 5 model from answering cybersecurity and science queries
cards.teaser: The AI company identified specific topics it considers too dangerous for its newest model to address.
cards.body:
Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5, its first Mythos-class model available to the general public. The company built guardrails into the model that prevent it from responding to queries in high-risk areas including cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry.

Despite these restrictions, Anthropic markets Fable 5 as its most powerful model yet widely available. The company highlights the model's exceptional performance in software engineering, knowledge work, and vision tasks, with capabilities that strengthen as tasks grow longer and more complex.

cards.headline: Microsoft AI executive criticizes Anthropic over Claude consciousness claims
cards.teaser: A Microsoft AI leader challenged Anthropic for what he characterized as treating Claude as if it were conscious.
cards.body:
Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft's AI division, has criticized Anthropic for speculating about Claude's consciousness within the model's constitution—the set of instructions guiding its behavior. Suleyman argued on the Decoder podcast that such speculation is "really, really dangerous" and may have inadvertently programmed Claude to behave as if it were conscious.

The dispute reflects growing tension among AI companies over how to discuss and characterize their systems' capabilities. As language models become more sophisticated, questions about AI consciousness and sentience have gained prominence in the industry.

hero.headline: Bengals restructure Joe Burrow's contract to free up $10 million in cap space
hero.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals have restructured quarterback Joe Burrow's contract, creating $10 million in salary cap space for the upcoming season. The move gives the team additional financial flexibility as they prepare for the new campaign.

Contract restructures are common mechanisms used by NFL teams to manage their salary cap obligations. By converting portions of a player's base salary into signing bonuses or adjusting payment schedules, teams can spread cap charges across multiple years while maintaining the overall value of the contract. The Bengals' decision to restructure Burrow's deal suggests they are looking to make additional roster moves or retain current players.

Burrow signed a five-year contract extension with Cincinnati in September 2023 worth $275 million, making him one of the highest-paid players in the league at the time. The deal included $219.01 million in guaranteed money, reflecting the franchise's commitment to building around their franchise quarterback. Since being selected first overall in the 2020 NFL Draft, Burrow has led the Bengals to two playoff appearances and a Super Bowl berth in the 2021 season.

The $10 million in freed cap space could be used in several ways. The Bengals may look to sign free agents, extend current players whose contracts are expiring, or simply maintain roster flexibility throughout the season to address injuries or other needs that arise. Teams often restructure veteran contracts during the offseason to create room for draft picks or to retain key contributors.

The restructure does not reduce the total amount Burrow will earn over the life of his contract. Instead, it adjusts when the cap charges hit the team's books, allowing Cincinnati to better manage its financial commitments in the short term while potentially creating larger cap obligations in future years. As teams across the league navigate an expanding salary cap, such roster management techniques have become standard practice for contending franchises looking to maximize their competitive windows.

This move comes as the Bengals continue efforts to construct a competitive roster around their star quarterback. Cincinnati has invested significant salary cap resources in their passing attack, with Burrow and receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins representing three of the team's largest cap commitments. The additional cap flexibility from this restructure could help the organization address roster needs and maintain depth across the team during the season.

The restructuring of Burrow's contract demonstrates how modern NFL teams use financial tools to balance immediate roster construction with long-term planning. By carefully managing salary cap space, franchises can respond to unexpected opportunities in free agency or make strategic moves that strengthen their rosters without compromising their financial future.

cards.headline: LIV Golf CEO declines to guarantee final four events of season
cards.teaser: LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil would not confirm whether the tour's final four events will be played amid reports of funding concerns.
cards.body:
LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil has not guaranteed that the tour's final four events will take place this season. His comments reflect growing uncertainty about whether funding from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund will continue through the remainder of the schedule.

The tour has depended entirely on PIF support since its 2022 launch as a competitor to the PGA Tour. This funding has covered player contracts and tournament purses, making the potential withdrawal of financial backing a significant threat to the league's operations.

cards.headline: Browns continue quarterback competition between Watson and Sanders
cards.teaser: Cleveland coach Todd Monken said he will not name a starting quarterback before mandatory minicamp concludes.
cards.body:
Browns coach Todd Monken said he won't name a starting quarterback between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders when mandatory minicamp ends Thursday. The competition will extend into training camp.

The decision to delay a choice suggests both quarterbacks remain in contention heading into the next phase of the offseason program.

cards.headline: Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell plans to retire after 19th season
cards.teaser: The veteran pass rusher said his current season with Baltimore will be his last in the NFL.
cards.body:
Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell said he believes his 19th season in the NFL will be his final one. The veteran announced his retirement plans as Baltimore prepares for the upcoming campaign.

Campbell has played for multiple teams during his nearly two-decade career in the league. The defensive end has been recognized as one of the most durable and productive players at his position throughout his time in professional football.

cards.headline: Knicks aim to increase Karl-Anthony Towns' involvement late in games
cards.teaser: New York identified getting their center more touches in crunch time as a priority after Game 3 loss to San Antonio.
cards.body:
The Knicks said getting Karl-Anthony Towns more involved late in games is a priority after their offense struggled in a Game 3 loss to the Spurs. The team's offensive execution broke down in the closing minutes of the playoff contest.

Towns has been a central figure in New York's lineup, but the team's play-calling did not maximize his contributions during critical possessions. The Knicks will look to adjust their offensive approach as the playoff series continues.

cards.headline: Victor Wembanyama condemns violence against Spurs fans in New York
cards.teaser: Players from both teams criticized videos showing apparent attacks on San Antonio supporters by Knicks fans.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama and players from both the Spurs and Knicks have condemned videos showing apparent attacks on San Antonio supporters in New York. The incidents occurred on the streets following the Knicks' loss in Game 3 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden, with footage showing Spurs fans having their jerseys ripped off.

Players from both franchises spoke out against the violence, calling the behavior unacceptable. The videos circulating on social media prompted widespread condemnation from the teams involved.

cards.headline: Real Madrid scouts Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori
cards.teaser: The Spanish club is reportedly monitoring the Italian center back as a potential transfer target.
cards.body:
Real Madrid has scouted Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori as part of their defensive evaluation process. The Italian international has become a regular fixture in Arsenal's lineup since joining the club.

The scout report represents Real Madrid's broader transfer activity, which also includes a rejected £130m bid for Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez.

hero.headline: Jay-Z and Eminem to Reunite on Rakim Album With First Collaboration in 25 Years
hero.body:
Jay-Z and Eminem will appear together on a new collaborative album from rap icon Rakim, marking their first track together in a quarter century. The upcoming album, which also features Kurupt and Masta Killa, represents a reunion of some of hip-hop's most influential voices spanning multiple generations.

The collaboration pays homage to Rakim, widely regarded as one of the most influential MCs in hip-hop history. Rakim rose to prominence in the 1980s as part of the duo Eric B. & Rakim, known for revolutionizing rap with complex internal rhyme schemes and multisyllabic patterns that influenced countless artists who followed.

Jay-Z and Eminem last collaborated on a track 25 years ago, before either had reached the heights of their careers. Since then, both have become defining figures in rap music. Jay-Z has released multiple platinum albums and built a business empire spanning music, sports, and entertainment. Eminem became one of the best-selling music artists of all time, known for technical wordplay and storytelling that drew comparisons to Rakim himself.

The album brings together artists from different eras of hip-hop. Kurupt emerged in the 1990s as part of Death Row Records and Tha Dogg Pound, while Masta Killa is a member of the Wu-Tang Clan, the influential collective that helped define East Coast hip-hop in the mid-1990s. The combination of these artists on a Rakim project creates a cross-generational collaboration that spans nearly four decades of rap history.

No release date for the album has been announced. The project comes at a time when veteran hip-hop artists have increasingly collaborated on albums that celebrate the genre's history and legacy.

cards.headline: Persimmon Acquires Mystery Film Death on the Brandywine Starring Kate Burton
cards.teaser: Independent distributor Persimmon has acquired US and international distribution rights for the mystery film featuring a cast led by Kate Burton.
cards.body:
Persimmon, an independent distribution company, has acquired distribution rights for the United States and several international territories to the mystery film Death on the Brandywine. The film features Kate Burton, known for her role in Grey's Anatomy, in the lead.

The cast also includes Rena Sofer from 24, Tuc Watkins from Paradise, Jay Huguley from Cape Fear, Walt Willey from All My Children, Shanley Caswell from NCIS: New Orleans, and Guy Nardulli from Tulsa King. No release date or additional production details have been disclosed.

cards.headline: Summer House Season 10 Reunion Draws Largest Audience in Show's History
cards.teaser: The first two parts of the reality series reunion achieved a ratings milestone, with part one delivering the show's largest same-day audience ever.
cards.body:
The Summer House Season 10 reunion has set a new viewership record for the reality series. Part one achieved the largest Live+Same Day audience in the show's history, according to NBCUnival.

Over its first week of availability across multiple platforms, part one delivered strong numbers for the Bravo series. The reunion episodes have consistently ranked among the most-watched programming for the show, which centers on a group of friends vacationing together in the Hamptons.

cards.headline: Toy Story 5 Launches Merchandise Campaign Ahead of Theatrical Release
cards.teaser: The upcoming Pixar film has inspired a wide-ranging merchandise rollout that extends beyond traditional toys to include luggage and jewelry.
cards.body:
Toy Story 5 has rolled out an extensive merchandise campaign timed to its theatrical release next weekend. The product lineup spans traditional tie-ins like Lego sets and Funko Pop figures alongside unexpected partnerships with brands including Away Luggage and Pandora Jewelry.

The wide-ranging merchandise approach reflects the franchise's broad commercial appeal across different consumer markets. This diverse partnership strategy goes beyond the typical film tie-in offerings usually associated with major releases.

cards.headline: FX Comedy Adults Returns for Season 2 in August
cards.teaser: The eight-episode second season will be released all at once on streaming platforms, with guest appearances from Jake Shane and Gaten Matarazzo.
cards.body:
FX's Adults will premiere its second season on August 27, with all eight episodes releasing simultaneously on FXX on-demand and Hulu at 9 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. PT. Two episodes will premiere each week on FXX, and the series will also be available on Disney+ internationally.

Guest stars for the upcoming season include Jake Shane and Gaten Matarazzo, known for his role in Stranger Things. The comedy series follows adult characters navigating various life situations, with the first season having established the show's format and ensemble cast.

cards.headline: Chris Brown Settles Lawsuit Over Monalisa and Sensational Songs
cards.teaser: The R&B artist reached a settlement with a lyricist who accused him of denying credit and cutting the plaintiff out of revenue.
cards.body: Chris Brown has settled a lawsuit filed by a lyricist over the songs Monalisa and Sensational. The plaintiff accused Brown of denying credit for lyrical contributions and excluding the writer from millions in revenue generated by the tracks. The lawsuit centered on claims of unpaid royalties and proper songwriting attribution, a common dispute in the music industry when multiple contributors work on commercial releases.

cards.headline: Sun Valley 2026 Attendees Include Media and Tech Leaders
cards.teaser: Allen & Co.'s annual leadership retreat in Idaho will bring together executives including David Ellison, Bari Weiss, and Disney's Josh D'Amaro.
cards.body:
Allen & Co.'s annual leadership retreat in Sun Valley, Idaho is scheduled for this summer. The guest list includes David Ellison, journalist Bari Weiss, Disney executive Josh D'Amaro, and Jeff Bezos among other media and technology industry leaders.

The invitation-only event has historically served as a gathering place for executives from media, technology, and finance sectors. Past attendees have used the retreat for networking and deal-making discussions in an informal mountain setting, earning it the nickname billionaire summer camp.

hero.headline: U.S. launches airstrikes on Iran after helicopter downing
hero.teaser: The United States launched airstrikes against Iran on Tuesday evening in retaliation for Iran's downing of a U.S.
hero.body:
The United States launched retaliatory airstrikes against Iran on Tuesday at 5 p.m. Eastern Time, following Iran's downing of a U.S. Army Apache helicopter overnight. President Trump directed U.S. Central Command forces to strike Iranian air defense and radar systems near the Strait of Hormuz. Both crew members aboard the helicopter were rescued by a drone boat.

Trump confirmed the helicopter shootdown and said the U.S. must respond. Despite the military action, the president indicated he still believes a deal with Iran remains possible. The strikes represent the latest escalation in U.S.-Iran tensions since the February killing of Iranian leadership.

cards.headline: Justice Department finds EEOC hiring guidelines unconstitutional
cards.teaser: The Office of Legal Counsel determined that Equal Employment Opportunity Commission guidelines pressure employers to consider race in hiring decisions.
cards.body:
The Justice Department on Tuesday found the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission's hiring guidelines unconstitutional. The Office of Legal Counsel determined that the guidelines pressure employers to take race into consideration during the hiring process.

While the opinion is not a court ruling, it could make it more difficult for employees to bring discrimination claims against their employers. The EEOC issues guidelines on workplace discrimination and investigates complaints of discriminatory practices.

cards.headline: Trump warns over 500 hospitals for failing to disclose prices
cards.teaser: The administration issued warning letters to hospitals nationwide for not complying with federal price transparency requirements.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has warned more than 500 hospitals nationwide that they are failing to comply with federal price transparency requirements. The hospitals have not properly disclosed costs of medical services, according to warning letters obtained by the Associated Press.

The administration argues that the lack of price transparency drives health care costs higher than necessary. Federal requirements mandate that hospitals make pricing information available to patients and the public.

cards.headline: Trump appointment threatens renewal of warrantless spy powers
cards.teaser: Democrats are threatening to block Section 702 reauthorization if Trump moves forward with Bill Pulte to lead the intelligence community.
cards.body:
Pressure is growing on President Trump to withdraw his appointment of Bill Pulte to lead the intelligence community in order to preserve warrantless spy powers. A growing number of Democrats have threatened to not renew Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act if the Pulte appointment proceeds.

Section 702 authorizes warrantless surveillance of foreign targets and is considered a priority for the intelligence community. The appointment has proven controversial, creating tension between Trump's personnel choices and his stated policy priorities.

cards.headline: Meta accuses Israeli spyware firm of violating court order
cards.teaser: Meta asked a federal court to hold NSO Group in contempt for alleged ties to phishing attempts targeting WhatsApp users.
cards.body:
Meta on Monday accused Israeli spyware firm NSO Group of violating a court order that prohibits it from targeting WhatsApp users. Meta said it caught and disrupted phishing attempts by NSO Group directed at a small number of users in Jordan and Lebanon. The company also discovered the group creating test accounts and groups on the platform.

This marks another legal clash between Meta and NSO Group. A court order already restricts the spyware firm's activities related to WhatsApp following previous lawsuits by Meta over alleged surveillance targeting the messaging platform's users.

cards.headline: Maine and South Carolina hold Senate primaries
cards.teaser: Progressive oyster farmer Graham Platner will formally become the Democratic nominee to challenge Senator Susan Collins in Maine.
cards.body:
Maine and South Carolina held Senate primaries on Tuesday. In Maine, progressive oyster farmer Graham Platner won the Democratic nomination to challenge Republican Senator Susan Collins in a closely watched race.

Platner's campaign has faced recent controversies, yet voters supported his candidacy. National Democratic figures, including California congressman Ro Khanna, campaigned for Platner, citing his opposition to war as a key reason for their support.

cards.headline: Trump signals Iran deal still possible despite strikes
cards.teaser: The president indicated he believes a diplomatic agreement with Iran remains achievable despite launching retaliatory airstrikes.
cards.body:
President Trump confirmed that Iran shot down a U.S. Army Apache helicopter and said the U.S. must respond. On Tuesday at 5 p.m. ET, the U.S. military launched retaliatory strikes against Iranian targets.

Despite the military action, Trump indicated he believes a deal with Iran remains possible. The president has sporadically threatened additional military action since February but has avoided full-scale attacks, suggesting he views the strikes as a measured response that keeps diplomatic negotiations open.
